Re.: Outcome of Board Meeting and disclosure under Regulation 30 of Schedule III of the Securities
and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015,
as amended (“Listing Regulations”) with respect to further updates in relation to the proposed
investment into Brahma AI Holdings Limited (“Brahma Holdings”) and Brahma AI Services India
Limited (“Brahma India”), material subsidiaries of the Company, by way of subscription to
compulsorily convertible preference shares (“CCPS”) of Brahma Holdings by Multiples Private
Equity Gift Fund IV and of Brahma India by Multiples Private Equity Fund IV (collectively referred
to as “Multiples”)
Dear Sir/ Madam,
This is further to our disclosure dated September 23, 2026 (“Earlier Disclosure”) in relation to the
proposed investment by Multiples in Brahma Holdings and Brahma India, material subsidiaries of Prime
Focus Limited (“Company”), respectively (“Proposed Transaction”).
The Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held today, i.e. October 15, 2026, has, inter alia,
considered the following and approved / recommended the same:
1.

Subject to the provisions of applicable laws including approval of the members of the Company in
accordance with provisions of Regulation 23(4) of the Listing Regulations, the Board considered and
recommended the following matters in relation to the Proposed Transaction:
(a)

The material related party transaction between DNEG S.à.r.l (“DNEG Parent”), an unlisted
material subsidiary of the Company and Brahma Holdings, a material unlisted subsidiary of
the Company, for entering into the Ancillary Framework Deed with Brahma Holdings, Brahma
India, Multiples, pursuant to which DNEG Parent shall, inter alia, undertake indemnity
obligations in favour of Brahma Holdings, (for itself and as agent for each Brahma Group
Company (as defined in the Framework Deed)), for any Indemnified Liability (as defined in
the Framework Deed), for such amounts as may become payable from time to time in
accordance with the Framework Deed;

(b)

The material related party transaction between Double Negative Holdings Limited (“DNEG
Holdings”), an unlisted subsidiary of the Company and Brahma Holdings, for entering into a
shareholders agreement relating to Brahma Holdings with Brahma Holdings, Multiples, and

 Mr. Prabhu Narasimhan (“SHA”) under which each shareholder of Brahma Holdings
(including DNEG Holdings) that is a party to the SHA has agreed to indemnify and hold
harmless Brahma Holdings and each Group Company (as defined in the SHA) on an after-Tax
basis from and against any liability with respect to any Tax required to be withheld, deducted
or paid on behalf of or with respect to such shareholder under applicable law, including any
interest, penalties, or costs arising therefrom; and
(c)

2.

The material related party transaction for platform license arrangement between DNEG Parent
and Brahma Holdings for inter alia licensing of Brahma AI Platform together with related
models, workflows, interfaces, documentation, updates, upgrades, releases and other
components for the annual fees which is expected to result in the transaction value exceeding
the applicable materiality thresholds under Regulation 23(4) of the Listing Regulations.

To convene an Extra Ordinary General Meeting of the members of the Company (“EOGM”) on
Saturday, November 7, 2026, through Video Conferencing / Other Audio Visual Means for and
reviewed, considered and approved the draft notice of the EOGM of the Company for:
(a) consideration and approval of the Proposed Transaction (to be read with the Earlier Disclosure)
resulting in cessation of control over Brahma Holdings and consequently, over Brahma India, the
unlisted material subsidiaries of the Company pursuant to the subscription by Multiples to CCPS of
Brahma Holdings and Brahma India, and transfer of the shares in Brahma India held by DNEG Parent
to Brahma Holdings, respectively, by way of special resolution in accordance with Regulation 24(5)
of the Listing Regulations; and (b) consideration and approval of the material related party
transactions as detailed above in Sr. No. (1).

The Meeting of the Board commenced at 7:30 p.m. and concluded at 8:15 p.m.
Kindly take the above on your record and acknowledge receipt of the same.
Thanking you.
For Prime Focus Limited

Kabra Extrusiontechnik Reports a Step-Change in Q2 FY27: Revenue up 64.2%,
EBITDA up 116.0% and PAT up 1,084.8% YoY
Q2 FY27 revenues up 64.2% YoY to ₹ 2,210 Mn; EBITDA up 116.0% YoY to ₹ 194 Mn;

Mumbai, October 15, 2026: Kabra Extrusiontechnik Ltd. (BSE - 524109, NSE - KABRAEXTRU, ISIN:
INE900B01029), a fast-scaling battery pack and energy storage solutions company through its Geon
division and a long-established manufacturer of plastic extrusion machinery, has announced its
results for the second quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026. Growth was led by Geon,
which more than doubled year-on-year and now contributes three-fourths of consolidated revenues,
translating into a sharp expansion in profitability across both the quarter and the half year.

Geon – Building a Multi-Segment New-Energy Platform:
Electric Mobility
▪

Collaboration with a Top Three Indian Two-Wheeler Manufacturer: Geon received a Letter
of Intent from one of India's top three two-wheeler manufacturers and will collaborate with the
customer on the development and supply of two battery programmes, along with the
establishment of a dedicated plant in South India

▪

Battery-Pack Nomination in Vietnam: Geon secured a Letter of Nomination from the top
passenger vehicle manufacturer in Vietnam for the development and supply of battery packs,
marking an important step towards expanding its global presence in the electric-mobility
ecosystem and strengthening its advanced-battery capabilities in international markets

▪

Entry into High-Voltage Battery Packs for Passenger Cars: The move broadens Geon's
addressable mobility portfolio and takes its battery capabilities into the passenger car segment
with cell-to-pack technology
Energy Storage Systems (ESS)

▪

Commissioning of a 10 MW / 20 MWh BESS at Phalodi, Rajasthan: Commissioned under the
requirements of Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Limited, the project represents an
important extension of the Company's new-energy capabilities beyond EV battery applications
into stationary, grid-connected battery storage

▪

Commissioning of a Second 10 MW / 20 MWh BESS at Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, on an EPC Basis:
Geon successfully executed and commissioned the project on a turnkey EPC basis, with a scope
encompassing detailed engineering and design, procurement and supply of equipment, and
installation, testing and commissioning, in accordance with the Rajasthan Integrated Clean Energy
Policy, 2024. The system is designed to support efficient energy management, grid stability and
the effective integration of renewable energy. With this, Geon has commissioned 20 MW / 40 MWh
of grid-scale storage in Rajasthan across two projects, reinforcing its ability to deliver utility-scale
BESS on a turnkey EPC basis

▪

BESS Technical Services at the Khavda Renewable Energy Hub, Gujarat: Phase 1 of 2.88 GWh
– among India's largest utility-scale battery storage deployments – was successfully
commissioned in June 2026, within five months of project initiation, with Geon serving as the
nodal agency responsible for complete system integration, execution, testing and commissioning,

including power conditioning systems, transformers and energy management systems. Following
Geon's successful delivery of the Phase 1 deliverables, the client has initiated Phase 2 of 7.5 GWh
International & Corporate Development
▪

Incorporation of an Overseas Wholly Owned Subsidiary in the UAE: On October 5, 2026, the
Company incorporated Geon International FZ-LLC, a Free Zone Limited Liability Company in the
Ras Al Khaimah Economic Zone (RAKEZ), United Arab Emirates, as a 100% wholly owned
subsidiary with an initial subscribed share capital of AED 3.9 Mn. The entity will act as the
intermediary holding company for the Company's international business and is intended to hold
the proposed subsidiary in Vietnam, which will set up a battery pack manufacturing facility,
formalising the structure for Geon's international expansion

▪

Fund Raise to Fuel Growth Ambition: The preferential issue of ₹ 1,410 Mn strengthens the
balance sheet and funds the Company's next growth phase, substantially broadening the
addressable landscape for Geon

the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, as recommended by the Audit
Committee, along with the Limited Review Report(s) of the Statutory Auditors, which are
attached. The said financial results are being uploaded on the website of the Company
www.kolsite.com and will be published in newspapers as per the requirements of the
Listing Regulations.

designated as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) – Extrusion Division, from the services of the
Company with effect from October 22, 2026.

circular No. SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD2/CIR/P/0155 dated November 11, 2024, SEBI Master

Dear Sir/Madam,
Subject: Outcome of the Board Meeting _ Disclosure regarding proposed fund-raising
Pursuant to Regulation 30 and other applicable provisions of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, we wish to inform you that the Board of Directors of
Viviana Power Tech Limited (“the Company”), at its meeting held on October 15, 2026,
comprehensively deliberated upon the proposed fund-raising initiative through the issuance of fully
convertible warrants on a preferential basis.
After an exhaustive evaluation of the various fund-raising avenues available to the Company, including
a comparative assessment of their respective merits, limitations, capital-raising implications, potential
dilution, shareholder participation and alignment with the Company's long-term strategic objectives,
the Board of Directors, after due consideration and detailed deliberations, unanimously decided
not to proceed with the proposed issuance of fully convertible warrants on a preferential basis.
The Board's decision reflects a prudent assessment of the Company's anticipated financial
requirements, future business prospects, capital structure and strategic priorities. The decision
underscores the Company's commitment to exercising financial prudence, evaluating available
alternatives objectively and ensuring that its capital management strategy remains aligned with its longterm business objectives and the interests of its shareholders.
The Company remains committed to strengthening its financial foundation, supporting its business
expansion and operational requirements, and adopting a disciplined approach to capital management
with a view to creating sustainable long-term value for its shareholders and other stakeholders.
The meeting of the Board of Directors commenced at 4.30 pm and concluded at 6.00 pm.
You are requested to take the above information on record.
For Viviana Power Tech Limited
